Even ignoring that, it keeps the import-name bail in classify(), so the TS import-shadowed api: Foo case suppresses R3 but degrades to NameOnly instead of recovering the unpoisoned local Foo type. Its recovery byte cutoff also applies to Rust/Go, violating the strict Python/JS/TS gate. Arm B has the better root-cause model: ReceiverClassification distinguishes Unmaterialized, MaterializedPoisoned, and Recovered; Python/JS/TS scan for a local binding before leaving R3/R3b live; poisoned bindings suppress R3/R3b and fall to residue; unpoisoned bindings still recover Exact owner lookup. Its scope recovery is byte-aware for Python/JS/TS and skips nested class scopes while preserving Rust/Go line behavior. Arm B's tests reproduce both false-Exact cases and the scope recovery bug and would fail on the pre-fix behavior.
